title: Qualcomm Has Eyes On The AI Inference Datacenter With HBC And AI250
gist: Qualcomm says first-generation HBC silicon (LPDDR stack over a full AI accelerator die) has been validated in the lab at 18x LPDDR bandwidth and 5x HBM4's Tbps-per-watt, framing near-memory compute as its answer to the inference 'memory wall' and its differentiator versus Nvidia. HBC will anchor the Dragonfly AI250 (sampling H1 2027) and Dragonfly Rack, with AI300 samples in 2028.

insights.claim: Qualcomm argues AI inference and agentic AI performance increasingly depend less on a processor's compute speed and more on how quickly data can be fed to the calculation, a problem it calls the memory wall.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Shifts competitive focus in inference silicon from FLOPs to memory bandwidth and data movement.

insights.claim: Qualcomm frames three inference strategies: hold the model in fast on-chip memory, use stacked HBM next to a processor, or (its choice) near-memory computing via HBC that moves compute to the memory.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Useful taxonomy for comparing SRAM-heavy, HBM-GPU and near-memory inference vendors.
